NU.PAR: NU.PAR (the signs NU and PAR, the BAR sign) — a second class of dedicated woman named beside the qadištum (§181); given as the signs only, with no reading and no translation, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, untranslated
SAL-sign: SAL — the woman-sign standing alone after NIN.AN in §178–179 (Harper’s ŠAL(?)); given as the sign and no more, since a lone SAL is read by some later editions as a class of priestess, UNCERTAIN; not read as a word here (compare zinništum and aššat, where SAL is read) · Sumerogram, untranslated
SIG.BA: SIG.BA (SIG + BA) — “wool ration” (SIG wool, BA allowance), one of the three rations of §178–179 (Harper writes ŠIG.BA); the Akkadian word behind it is not read, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, untranslated
Ì.BA: Ì.BA (Ì + BA; Harper writes NI.BA) — “oil ration” (Ì oil, BA allowance), one of the three rations of §178–179; the Akkadian word behind it is not read, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, untranslated
ŠE.BA: ŠE.BA (ŠE + BA) — “grain ration” (ŠE grain, BA allowance), one of the three rations of §178–179; the Akkadian word behind it is not read, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, untranslated
emūqum: strength, power; the means of a house: emūq (e-mu-uq, no ending written, construct state “strength of”) in kīma emūq zittiša “in proportion to the strength of her share” and kīma emūq bīt abim “in proportion to the means of her father’s house” · noun
ēma: wherever; with the sense “to whomever”, before a clause with its verb in the subjunctive: ēma (e-ma) in warkassa ēma eliša ṭābu nadānam “her estate, wherever (to whomever) it pleases her, to give” · adverb / conjunction
mazûm-Š: UNCERTAIN verb, the root not settled; read from the context as “to let (her) have her fill, as much as she wishes”: ušamziši (u-ša-am-zi-ši) “he has (not) let her have”, Š-stem preterite + -ši “her”; uštamziši (uš-tam-zi-ši) “he has let her have”, Š-stem perfect + -ši · Š-stem verb
qadištum: a consecrated woman, a class of woman dedicated to a god, written {šal}NU.GIG (SAL + NU + GIG; Harper qadištu): qadištam “a qadištum” (accusative); her exact status is not settled, UNCERTAIN · noun
zikrum-priestess: zikrum (zi-ik-ru-um) — the name of a class of woman named beside the priestess in §178–180; it is not zikrum “name” of the prologue, and what the class was is not known, UNCERTAIN · noun
šalšum: a third, one third (written IGI.3.GAL, three signs: IGI, the numeral 3, GAL): before a following noun šalšat “one third of”, a reconstructed construct form, marked (?) in the gloss: šalšat ablūtiša “a third of her heirship” · numeral / fraction, Sumerogram
šarāqum-give: to give as a gift, to bestow (a dowry); kept apart from šarāqum “to steal”: išruq (preterite “he gave”) with -šim “to her”: išruqšim (iš-ru-uq-ši-im; iš-[ru]-uq-ši-im with the RU lost on the plate; iš-ru-uq-šim with the single sign ŠIM), šeriqtam lā išruqšim “he has not given her a dowry”; with the subjunctive -u in a ša-clause, išruqušim (iš-ru-qu₂-ši-im) “(whom) he gave her”; išarraqūšima (i-šar-ra-qu₂-ši-ma) “they shall give her, and”, present plural + -ši + -ma · verb, G-stem
ṭâbum-D: to make good, to content, satisfy (literally “make the heart good”): libbaša uṭabbū (u-ṭa-ab-bu) “they shall content her”, D-stem present plural; uṭṭibbū (uṭ-ṭi-ib-bu) “they have contented (her)”, D-stem perfect, the form UNCERTAIN because of the doubled b · verb, D-stem

__broaden__.ugbabtum: UNCERTAIN: a priestess, written ŠAL.NIN.AN (Harper aššatum NIN.AN; NIN.AN is later written NIN.DINGIR, “lady of the god”); Harper gives no reading and translates only “a priestess”, later editions read ugbabtum, and the ŠAL may be only the woman-sign. The reading rests on the sign group and the context, not on a spelled word · here (§127) NIN.AN alone, with no ŠAL before it: ugbabtim “of a priestess”, still read ugbabtum, UNCERTAIN as before (Harper gives no reading) · in §178–179 NIN.AN followed by a separate SAL (Harper’s ŠAL(?)) read as its own word, not as part of the title: ugbabtum, still UNCERTAIN, the SAL left unread (see SAL-sign)
__broaden__.ṭuppum: the clay tablet; the deed: ṭuppašu iḫḫeppi “his tablet shall be smashed” — the sale annulled physically · ṭuppam (dup-pa-am, accusative), ṭuppim (dup-pi₂-im, genitive) “the tablet”: the tablet a father writes for his daughter, in which her dowry and her right to dispose of her estate are set down; kunukkam is the sealed one
__broaden__.šaṭārum: to write; to assign in writing, deed over (Harper: išaddar): ul išaddar “he shall not deed” · išṭuršum (iš-tur-šum) “he wrote for him”: kunukkam išṭuršum “he wrote him a sealed document” · išṭurušim (iš-tu-ru-ši-im, with the subjunctive -u in a ša-clause), išṭuršim (iš-tur-ši-im), išṭuršimma (iš-tur-ši-im-ma) “he wrote for her (and)”, preterite + -šim: ina ṭuppim ša išṭurušim “in the tablet which he wrote for her”, lā išṭuršimma “he has not written for her, and”
__broaden__.nadānum: to give, pay: inaddin, iddinam, iddinušum; nadānim “to give” · iddin “he gave”; ana kaspim nadānum “to sell”: inaddinūma (present, plural) “they shall sell, and …” · iddin, iddinu “he gave” (preterite; the subjunctive -u in a ša- or inūma clause); iddinma “he gave, and”; …in, …din in broken forms; inaddin “he shall give”: ana damqaršu inaddin “he shall give to his merchant” · ittadinma (it-ta-di-in-ma) “he has given, and” (perfect); inaddinu (i-na-ad-di-nu) “(which) he gives” (present, with the subjunctive -u) · ittandin (it-ta-an-di-in, perfect with an extra -n-) “he has handed over”: ana kiššātim ittandin “he handed over into service”; ittadin (it-ta-din) “he has given”, i.e. sold; ana maṣṣarūtim inaddin “he gives for safekeeping”; iddinūšumma “they gave him, and” · inaddin also of a woman, “she shall give” · inaddišši (i-na-ad-di-iš-ši) “he/she shall give her” (the n of the stem swallowed before -ši), of a sale: ana kaspim inaddišši “she may sell her”, ul inaddišši “she shall not sell her” · anaddin “I shall give”, with the n merged into the k of -kum: anaddikkum (a-na-ad-di-ik-kum) “I shall give (her) to you”; iddinu (id-di-nu) “(which) he gave”; iddinušum “he gave him” · nadānam (na-da-nam, infinitive accusative) “to give”: warkassa … nadānam “(that she may) give her estate” · iddišši (id-di-iš-ši) “he gave her”, preterite + -ši, the n written š: ana mutim iddišši “he gave her to a husband” · inaddinūši (i-na-ad-di-nu-ši) “they shall give her”, inaddinūšimma (i-na-ad-di-nu-šim-ma) “they shall give her, and”, ittadnūšimma (it-ta-ad-nu-ši-im-ma) “they have given her, and” (perfect plural + -šim + -ma) · iddinušim (id-di-nu-ši-im) “he gave her”, with the subjunctive -u in a ša-clause
__broaden__.-ma: and (clause-chaining particle); also “it is X that…” · “only, alone”, on a noun after ša: ša aḫḫīšama (aḫ-ḫi-ša-ma) “that of her brothers alone”; also “and” between verbs: izzazma, iššīma, išṭuršimma
__broaden__.libbum: heart · ana libbi “into”: ana libbi zittišu “into his share” · libbaša, libbiša (li-ib-ba-ša, li-ib-bi-ša) “her heart”: mala libbiša “as much as her heart wants”; libbaša uṭabbū “they shall make her heart good”, i.e. content her
__broaden__.-ši: her / it (3rd-person feminine singular suffix, on a verb): ukannūšima “they shall convict her”, inaddûši “they shall throw her”, iqallûši “they shall burn her” · iṣṣabassi (iṣ-ṣa-ba-az-zi) “it has seized her” (the t of the perfect + -ši said ss, spelled -zi) · on the present plural: imannûši “they shall count her”, ibaqqarūši “they shall claim against her” · on the Š-stem: ušērribši “he shall bring her in”, ušamṭaši “he has belittled her” · on a verb, the object “him” (UNCERTAIN): inaddûši “they shall throw him” (§155, the man being thrown into the water; the plate shows the sign ši, which elsewhere is “her”) · ilmassi (il-ma-zi) “he has known her”, ilmassima; iḫḫazzi “he shall take her”; išakkanūši “they shall set her (on a stake)” · on a verb of giving, “her”: iddišši (id-di-iš-ši) “he gave her”, inaddinūši “they shall give her”, išarraqūšima “they shall give her, and” · on the Gtn: ittanaššiši (it-ta-na-aš-ši-ši) “he shall keep supporting her”
__broaden__.eqlum: field (written A.ŠÀ): eqelšu “his field” — the fief-land this whole block protects · bound form eqel (eqel itêšu “his neighbour’s field”; eqel ušākilu “the field he grazed”) · eqlam (A.ŠÀ, accusative) “the field”, eqlša (A.ŠÀ-ša) “her field”: eqlša u kirâša “her field and her orchard”
__broaden__.kirûm: orchard, garden (written {giš}SAR, the KIRI₆ sign): kirāšu “his orchard” · kirâm (accusative), kirâša (written {giš}KIRI₆, the -ša written out) “her orchard”: eqlam kirâm “the field, the orchard”
__broaden__.aḫum-brother: brother (aḫum): aḫḫū (aḫ-ḫu) “brothers” (nominative plural), aḫīšunu (a-ḫi-šu-nu) “their brother” (aḫum + -šunu “their”) · aḫḫūša (aḫ-ḫu-ša) “her brothers” (nominative plural + -ša), aḫḫīša (aḫ-ḫi-ša) “of her brothers” (genitive plural): ša aḫḫīšama “that of her brothers alone”, itti aḫḫīša “with her brothers”
__broaden__.kīma: like, as · as, like; with a verb in the subjunctive: kīma ubbalu “as he brings (it)” · according to: kīma ṣimdat šarrim “according to the king’s schedule” · “since, when”, before a stative: kīma mimmûšu lā ḫalqu “since his goods are not lost” · “in proportion to”: kīma emūq zittiša “in proportion to the strength of her share”, kīma emūq bīt abim “in proportion to the means of her father’s house”
__broaden__.našûm: to bear, carry: ittanašši “he shall bear (the penalty)” · našû (na-šu-u, stative with the subjunctive -u) “(that) he carried”: mimma ša našû “anything that he carried” · ittanaššiši (it-ta-na-aš-ši-ši, Gtn present + -ši) “he shall keep carrying (supporting) her” · iššīma (iš-ši-ma) “he has lifted (her), and”: ana ilim iššīma “he has dedicated (her) to a god”, literally “lifted up to a god”; the sense “dedicated” is UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.akālum: to eat; infinitive akālum “eating, food”: akālim “of eating”, in ša akālim ibašši “there is food” (literally “something of eating”) · with a possession as object or alone, “to have the use of” (a house, an estate), literally “to eat it”: ikkal (i-ik-ka-al, present) in adi balṭat ikkal “as long as she lives she shall eat (have the use of it)”; the sense “have the use of” is UNCERTAIN · ikkal also written ì-kal (the sign NI read ì, then KAL): adi balṭat ikkal “as long as she lives she shall have the use of it”
__broaden__.šanûm: another, a second one: ana šanîm “to another”, šanûm “another man” · feminine šanītum “another (woman)”: šanītam, šanītim (ša-ni-tam, ša-ni-tim), in the accusative and genitive · šaniam (ša-ni-a-am, accusative) “another”: šaniam ul uppal “nor shall she pay another (?)”, UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.apālum: to answer; to satisfy, pay (a creditor): ippalma (present, with -ma) “he shall pay, and” · uppal (u-up-pa-al, present, the vowel pattern unusual) “she shall pay”, in šaniam ul uppal, UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.ablūtum: sonship, the status of a son (Harper’s word, from ablum “son”): ina ablūtim (ab-lu-tim) “from sonship”; nasāḫim ina ablūtim “to cast out of sonship” · ablūssa (ab-lu-za), ablūtiša (ab-lu-ti-ša) “her heirship”, the status or share of an heir (not “sonship” here, the heir being a daughter): ablūssa ša aḫḫīšama “her heirship belongs to her brothers alone”; šalšat ablūtiša “a third of her heirship”
__broaden__.kunukkum: seal; sealed document · kunukkam (ku-nu-kam, ku-nu-uk-kam, the UG sign read uk) “a sealed tablet”, accusative: kunukkam išṭuršim “he has written her a sealed tablet”
__broaden__.baqārum: to claim, make a claim against (Harper: BAKARU “to make claim”): ibaqqarūši (i-ba-qa₂-ru-ši, present plural, “they shall claim against her”) with -ši “her”; Harper prints the sign as ga, read qa₂ · ibaqqarūši also written i-ba-aq-qa₂-ru-ši (AK read aq + GA read qa₂): aḫḫūša ul ibaqqarūši “her brothers shall not make any claim against her”
__broaden__.mārtum: daughter (written DUMU+ti): mārtišu “his daughter” · mārassu (DUMU.SAL-zu, three signs DUMU + SAL + ZU, ZU for -ssu) “his daughter” · mārtaka (DUMU.SAL-ka) “your daughter”, mārtī (DUMU.SAL-i) “my daughter”, mārtim (DUMU.SAL, no ending written) “of the daughter”: abī mārtim “the father of the daughter” · mārtišu also written DUMU.SAL-šu (DUMU + SAL + ŠU) “his daughter”: ana mārtišu “to his daughter”
__broaden__.kallatum: bride (for a son), written with the Sumerogram É.GI₄.A, three signs and no ending written (Harper’s transliteration adds the ending, kal-lâtam): kallātam “a bride” · kallātim ({šal}É.GI₄.A) in §180: apparently a class of woman dedicated to a god, not “bride”; UNCERTAIN, the class cannot be defined
__broaden__.izuzzum: to stand; izzazzu “he stands (in service)” · izzaz, izzazma (i-za-az, i-za-az-ma) “she shall stand (take her place)”, of an heir’s share: zittam kīma aplim ištēn izzazma “she shall take a share like one heir, and”; ul izzaz “she shall have no share”; sense UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.aššatum: wife: ana aššatišu “to his wife” · aššassu (SAL-zu, ZU for -ssu) “his wife” · construct aššat (aš-ša-at) “wife of” before a genitive: aššat awīlim · aššatam, aššatim, aššatum, written SAL (the same sign as zinništum “woman”) or aš-ša-tam · aššātim (aš-ša-tim) “wives”, the plural (aššātim iḫuz “he has taken wives”; the signs could also spell the singular aššatim) · aššat (SAL, bare, construct) in aššat Marduk ša Bābilim “a wife of Marduk of Babylon”, the title of a priestess of the god; her status UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.ilkum: the fief-duty — service owed to the crown for land held: ilikšu illak “he shall perform his duty”; the keyword of §§26–41 · ilkam (il-kam, accusative) in ilkam ul illak “she shall not perform the fief-duty”
__broaden__.mutum: husband (short u; Harper “husband”; mūtum “death” is another word, spelled the same, so the sense rests on context): mutiša “her husband”, mussa “her husband” (written mu-za, -ša after the t), mut “husband of” (construct; mut libbiša “the husband of her heart”) · mutiša panîm / warkîm “her former / later husband”, with mutiša followed by an adjective in the genitive · mutim (mu-tim, genitive) “husband”: ana mutim iddišši “he gave her to a husband”
